title: Forgiveness of Sins
definition: Forgiveness of Sins is God's gracious removal of guilt and condemnation through the blood of Jesus Christ.
summary: Forgiveness of Sins is God's gracious removal of guilt through the blood of Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ has authority to forgive sins and secures forgiveness through His death and resurrection.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Forgiveness is not God pretending sin does not matter. It is God releasing the believer from guilt because Christ has borne sin and satisfied justice. This doctrine brings the wounded conscience to the cross and shows that pardon rests on Christ's blood, not on forgetfulness, excuses, or self-repair.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because guilt can either be denied or allowed to crush the soul. The Gospel does neither; it names sin truthfully and announces full pardon in Jesus. Forgiveness frees believers to walk in gratitude, confession, reconciliation, and peace with God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring specific sins into the light before the Lord instead of hiding them. Receive forgiveness on the basis of Christ, not your emotional sense of worthiness. Extend forgiveness to others as one who has been forgiven far more than you can repay.
